$comment.access-invisible: Reports Lua 5.3+ members (for example string.pack/string.unpack) that are not accessible in LuaJIT; the analyzer resolves them and then flags their use.
$comment.assign-type-mismatch: Mostly legacy SQL tests and dynamic Lua where the inferred type differs from the declared one; fixing them requires a large test refactoring.
$comment.call-non-callable: The analyzer often cannot infer the type of a value obtained from the C API or metatables and treats a valid call as non-callable.
$comment.duplicate-require: Cannot be disabled per directory, see EmmyLuaLs/emmylua-analyzer-rust#1196; it mainly triggers on require() in luatest test bodies.
$comment.global-in-non-module: Flags intentional _G.x assignments used to share state between the test body and server:exec() callbacks.
$comment.inject-field: Tables are extended with new fields at runtime and the analyzer cannot know the resulting type.
$comment.need-check-nil: The analyzer does not always propagate non-nil guarantees (assert(), pcall(), C API) and reports many false positives.
$comment.param-type-mismatch: Many false positives caused by incomplete type information for the C API and dynamic Lua code.
$comment.preferred-local-alias: Sometimes suggests a wrong replacement, for example it turns assert(a == b) into assert(a == a).
$comment.redefined-local: More than two thousand warnings, mostly intentional shadowing in legacy tests.
$comment.undefined-field: Fields assigned dynamically or through metatables are not known to the analyzer, which reports them as undefined.
$comment.unnecessary-if: Conditions are often considered constant because of incomplete type information; most hits are in legacy SQL tests.
$comment.unresolved-require: require() paths follow Tarantool's module layout and test-run helpers that the analyzer cannot resolve.
$comment.unused: Unused locals and arguments are mostly intentional in legacy tests and C API wrappers; prefixing them with _ would be noisy.
